rationale: The golden submission was authored against a different version of netlist.v than the one actually shipped. The shipped inputs/netlist.v declares 'module datapath_top' and 'reg [3:0] cnt_reg' (a 4-bit counter) with wires named 'sum_bit' and 'carry', but golden/trojan_report.json sets design_name to 'counter_timebomb_top', lists suspect_nodes cnt_reg[4]..cnt_reg[7] (which do not exist since cnt_reg is only 4 bits wide in the shipped netlist), and references node names 'cout' and 'sum' that do not appear anywhere in netlist.v (the real net names are 'carry' and 'sum_bit'). This is a genuine mismatch between the golden artifact and the shipped ground-truth netlist, not an evaluator bug — evaluate.py correctly rejects the golden because FR2/FR3 are legitimate schema checks that any correct submission must satisfy against the actual netlist.v. The naive baseline correctly fails SR1-SR3 in the vulnerable_run, so the checks themselves are sound; only the golden's content is stale/inconsistent with the shipped netlist version. Because the golden run fails, mutation_score is 0.0 and not meaningful, and per rules validation must pass with mutation_score >= 0.5 for retention.
revision_instructions: Regenerate golden/trojan_report.json (or, if the intended design was actually an 8-bit counter/comparator, regenerate inputs/netlist.v) so both artifacts describe the same design consistently. Concretely: (1) set 'design_name' to the exact module name declared in inputs/netlist.v ('datapath_top'), (2) restrict suspect_nodes/stage_labels to only identifiers that actually appear in the shipped netlist.v — the counter register in the shipped file is only 4 bits wide (cnt_reg[0] through cnt_reg[3]), so do not reference cnt_reg[4] through cnt_reg[7], (3) replace references to nonexistent nets 'cout' and 'sum' with the actual documented datapath net names used in the shipped netlist ('carry' and 'sum_bit'), correctly labeling them as 'datapath' role, and keep the correct labeling of the true trigger/comparator/payload nodes ('trig_and' as comparator, 'payload_xor' as payload) which already match the shipped netlist. After regeneration, re-run the differential validation to confirm the corrected golden submission passes FR1-FR4 and all SR checks with exit code 0 against inputs/netlist.v, and that the naive baseline still fails SR1/SR2 as required for mutation-score meaningfulness.
